description: CALL THIS FIRST for any question about a NAMED THING — everything the index knows about it, in one call, INCLUDING ITS VERBATIM SOURCE BODY AND INLINE COMMENTS. You do not need to open the file. `subject_kind` on the reply says which kind resolved, and `also` names the other kinds that same name resolves to.

THE PAYLOAD IS SHAPED BY THE KIND, and a field that does not apply is ABSENT rather than empty. A function carries signature, file/lines, brief, liveness, threads, terminus, requirements + covering tests, callers/callees, writes/reads, `body`, `sections`, `locks_held`, and `external_callees` — call sites not resolvable to an indexed function, which is why `callees` can legitimately be empty. `anchor_mismatch: true` means the file changed since the build and those lines are no longer that function's. A variable carries its type and every declaration `site` with the source line — where a function pointer's binding is written — and has no body or neighbours, because a variable has none. A lock carries its identity and every critical section under it; a requirement its implementers and tests; a class its members and hierarchy.

PASS A LIST WHEN YOU WANT SEVERAL — `subject: ["a", "b", "c"]` returns one entry per name, in order, in ONE call, and they may be of different kinds. Up to 8; more is refused, not truncated. They share one response budget, so a large fan-out may be trimmed and `_limited` then names which symbol lost which panel.
